subject: AtlasMap: upcoming data enrichment subscription and consolidation evaluation
messages:
From: Sam Park <sam@atlasmap.com>
To: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-28T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: AtlasMap subscription renewal and new tiering

Hi Hannah,

Quick note: your AtlasMap team subscription is set to auto-renew on 2026-04-01. We attached the renewal quote and an updated SLA addendum — pricing has shifted based on usage tiers (see attached). If you want to lock 2025 rates we can do a 12-month commitment by 2026-03-15. Otherwise, the account will renew month-to-month at the new list price.

We also added a new export utility (CSV) for bulk delivery and a proposed one-time migration credit for customers moving to our new unified schema.

Attachments: AtlasMap_Renewal_Quote_2026.pdf (pdf), atlasmap_sla_addendum_v2.docx (docx)

Let me know if you'd like a short call this week to walk the changes.

Thanks,
Sam Park
Partnerships — AtlasMap
sam@atlasmap.com

From: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T10:23:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: AtlasMap subscription renewal and new tiering

Folks — forwarding AtlasMap's renewal notice. Account auto-renews 04/01; vendor is offering a migration credit and a 12-mo rate lock if we sign by 03/15.

Context: AtlasMap is one of our third-party address/geolocation enrichment vendors. They power several internal enrichment pipelines for address normalization and reverse-geocoding. Usage has crept up ~30% YoY and cost per API call is a growing line item.

Asks:
- Neha: can you pull 2025 usage by product (Embedding ingestion vs. on-demand geocode) and show top 10 consumers?
- Marcus: quick cost delta comparing 12-mo lock vs month-to-month; also sketch competitor pricing (GridGeo, MapSift) — if you already have GridGeo data, include it.
- Lauren/Priyom: hold any auto-PO / renewals until we confirm approach; legal to scan AtlasMap SLA addendum for data retention/deletion clauses.

Goal: Decide whether to renew with AtlasMap, renegotiate, or consolidate with a competitor. I'd like a recommendation by 03/08 to inform our procurement action before their deadline.

Thanks — Hannah

Date: 2026-03-02T11:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: AtlasMap subscription renewal and new tiering

Hannah — I pulled the usage slices you asked for. High-level:
- Total enrichment calls (2025): 18.4M calls; 60% attributed to ingestion pipelines for entity resolution, 25% ad-hoc reverse-geocode, 15% test/dev.
- Cost center: 72% billed to Platform Integrations (Marcus's team), 18% to Growth experiments, remainder to Platform QA.
- Quality flags: we see higher failure/retry rates on international shipments (APAC) from AtlasMap's reverse-geocode; suspect coverage gaps.

I'll drop the CSV into the shared drive and paste the short table below. If we consider consolidation, the priority is to preserve the ingestion bulk-export capability and keep existing normalized schema.

Quick ask for Marcus: please incorporate usage growth (2024->2025) in your cost model; AtlasMap's one-time migration credit might offset onboarding for a competitor, but only if data mapping work is minimal.

NEHA

Attachment referenced: atlas_usage_2025_by_team.csv (csv)

From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-03T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: AtlasMap subscription renewal and new tiering — cost delta and competitor note

Summary from my side: I ran the numbers and sketched a quick comparison (attached).
- 12-mo commitment with AtlasMap (vendor quote): ~$85k/year after the migration credit vs month-to-month projected at ~$118k/year given current growth rates.
- Competitor GridGeo (pilot pricing): projected ~$72k/year but we expect ~2-3 weeks of mapping work and a nontrivial integration window for streaming ingestion.
- Risk premium for moving vendors (data gaps, perf regressions): estimate 10-15% engineering effort in first quarter of cutover.

Recommendation: Do NOT auto-renew immediately. Ask AtlasMap for a 60-day extension on the renewal deadline and a written export of all normalized records (CSV + schema). In parallel, run a 30-day pilot with GridGeo on a slice of traffic (we can throttle ingestion) to measure quality delta. If GridGeo meets quality and cost expectations, we consolidate; otherwise accept AtlasMap's 12-mo lock.

Attachment: redwood_cost_model_AtlasMap_vs_GridGeo.xlsx (xlsx)

Marcus

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-03T14:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: AtlasMap subscription renewal and new tiering — legal hold and SLA check

Thanks for the context. A few legal points:
- Please do not sign any amendment or rate lock that lacks explicit data deletion and export clauses. We need clear retention limits, a return-of-data workflow, and a certification of deletion for the old copies.
- The SLA addendum has standard uptime language but no strong data residency guarantees. If we intend to keep AtlasMap for US-only traffic, request a US region residency clause.
- Procurement: place a temporary hold on any auto-POs related to AtlasMap until legal confirms acceptable terms. Priyom, can you flag any scheduled renew payments for hold?

I'll review the SLA addendum in detail and propose marked changes to the vendor's doc. If AtlasMap refuses to extend the decision window, we should escalate to vendor ops and ask for a short-term amendment that preserves our export rights.

Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference

From: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sam Park <sam@atlasmap.com>, AtlasMap Sales <sales@atlasmap.com>, procurement@atlasmap.com
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-10T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Request to pause auto-renew and 60-day extension — AtlasMap account AM-3421

Sam / AtlasMap team — thanks for the heads up on the upcoming renewal. We value our work with AtlasMap but need more time to evaluate consolidation options and confirm legal/export requirements. Per internal review, please consider this an official request to pause the auto-renew for account AM-3421 and grant a 60-day extension on the renewal deadline (new proposed date: 2026-05-01).

Immediate asks:
1) Provide a machine-readable export of all normalized enrichment records tied to our account (CSV) plus the current schema mapping, within five business days.
2) Confirm in writing that AtlasMap will not begin any invoice or PO charging prior to the new renewal date if we accept the extension.
3) Share a customer-scoped statement on data residency and deletion obligations we can use to confirm compliance with our legal team.
4) If you can provide a one-time migration credit as mentioned in your earlier email, include the precise credit amount and terms.

Next steps on our side: Marcus will kick off a short pilot with a competitor (GridGeo) on a small traffic slice; Neha will share usage segments; Lauren/priyom will review contract edits and hold procurement actions until the extension is formalized. We will follow up with a proposed mutual action plan and an updated decision timeline in the next 7 days.

I have attached a short Mutual Action Plan template for the extension — please sign/acknowledge via DocuSign if you accept the 60-day hold. Link: https://docusign.example/sign/atlasmap-extend-60d

HubSpot ticket: https://hubspot.example/contacts/AM-3421

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Platform Partnerships — Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com

Attachments referenced: mutual_action_plan_AtlasMap.csv (csv)
